sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.1243/2013 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Neyyattinkara, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 15/05/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the first respondent/owner in the petition.

In this appeal,
the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 31/10/2013 at about 02:00 p.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-19-C-8737 through the Vilappilasala-Peyad public road and when he reached the place by name Kollamkonam, KSRTC bus bearing registration no.KL-15-3917 driven by the 2025:KER:59770 MACA NO. 462 OF 2020 second respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
A sum of 15,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle filed joint written statement denying negligence on the part of the latter.
The age, occupation and income of the claim petitioner were disputed.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
4. The third respondent/owner of the motorcycle in which the claim petitioner was riding remained ex parte.

5. The fourth respondent/insurer of the motorcycle in which the claim petitioner was riding filed written statement contending that the fourth respondent/insurer has no liability to pay compensation to the claim petitioner since there was no negligence on the part of the claim petitioner.
6. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A12 were marked on the side of the claim 2025:KER:59770 MACA NO. 462 OF 2020 petitioner.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the respondents.

7. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 6,89,000/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.

Aggrieved by the Award,
the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
8. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

sentences.text: 9. Heard both sides 10.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner 2025:KER:59770 MACA NO. 462 OF 2020 that the latter, a motor mechanic, was earning 12,000/-
per month.

However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 6,000/- only, which is quite low even going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.
Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.
Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is pointed out that he is a skilled worker and therefore the amount as claimed ought to have been granted by the Tribunal.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the first respondent/owner that the amount fixed by the Tribunal is quite reasonable and if at all this Court is inclined to enhance the same, it may be in accordance with the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra).
10.1. Going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the income of even a coolie is liable to be fixed at 9,000/- in the year 2013.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner,
relying on the dictum in Shivakumar M. v. Managing Director, Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation, (2017) 5 SCC 79, that even in the absence of any evidence, the Apex Court has fixed the notional income of a painter at 15,000/- per month.

entities.text: Shivakumar M. v. Managing Director, Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation, (2017) 5 SCC 79
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case 2025:KER:59770 MACA NO. 462 OF 2020 on hand, there is no evidence to prove the income of the claim petitioner.
In the claim petition, it is stated that he was a motor mechanic at the time of the incident.
In the written statement, respondents 1 and 2 have disputed the occupation of the claim petitioner.
In Shivakumar M. (Supra), the Apex Court granted the amount that was claimed, as the avocation of the claimant therein was never disputed.
In the case on hand, the avocation of the claim petitioner is disputed and therefore the aforesaid case cannot be applied to the facts of the present case.
However, taking into account the facts and circumstances of the case, I find that an amount of 10,000/- can be fixed as the notional income of the claim petitioner.
Percentage of permanent disability 11.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that when the doctor, as per Ext.A11 disability certificate, has assessed the disability as 22%, the Tribunal was unjustified in fixing the disability at 20%.

It is also submitted that the functional 2025:KER:59770 MACA NO. 462 OF 2020 disability ought to have been fixed much higher taking into account the nature of injuries sustained by the claim petitioner.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the first respondent/owner that the disability that needs to be fixed is the functional disability and taking into account the nature of injuries, the disability of 20% fixed is quite reasonable and that it does not call for any interference.

11.1. The materials on record show that following injuries were sustained by the claim petitioner:

11.2. Ext.A11 certificate issued by a single doctor reads thus:
"Paul John Victor alias Paul John 38 years, Kripa Theeram, Kalpadakuzhy, Punalal,
T h i r u v a n a n t h a p u r a m w a s a d m i t t e d i n M e d i c a l c o l l e g e H o s p i t a l ,
Thiruvananthapuram on 31/10/13 with IP No.987089/13 following an alleged road traffic accident.

entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: He sustained 2025:KER:59770 MACA NO. 462 OF 2020 Type III compound fracture of both bones of right leg, fracture of shaft of right femur and 2 part fracture of right proximal humerus.

He was treated by wound debridement,
external fixator on right leg, followed by phillos plating of humerus and interlocking nailing of right femur.
External fixator was replaced by Ilizarov fixator.
Skin grafting done.
He was discharged on 17/11/13.
Treatment continued as O.P.
He was again admitted on 24/1/14 with IP No.5438/14 with pin tract infection.
He was treated with antibiotics and discharged on 29/1/14.

He was again admitted on 18/2/14 with IP No.
11295/14.
External fixator removed and he was discharged with long leg cast.
Treatment continued as O.P.
At the time of examination on 4/10/17 he has the following features.
Scars on right leg with grafted skin Pus discharged from sinus on right femur.
Interlocking nail in situ.
Philos plate in situ.
Shortening of 1.5cm of right lower limb.
Wasting of 1cm of right thigh muscles Patient walks with limp.
Pain in right knee.
Flexion of right knee limited to 100 degrees.
Dorsiflexion and plantar flexion of right ankle limited 2025:KER:59770 MACA NO. 462 OF 2020 by 5 degrees.
Sensory dulling on right leg.
Flexion and external rotation of right hip limited by 10 degrees each.
Abduction of right shoulder limited to 100 degrees.
Difficulty in carrying weight.
Temporary disability of 100% for a period of Six months from date of injury.

3. Permanent disability of 22% (Twenty two percent) as per Mc Bride's scale Profession: Coolie"
In the light of the disability noted in Ext.A11 and in the light of the dictum in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343

sentences.text:
, I find that the Tribunal was right in fixing the functional disability as 20%
and hence the same does not call for any interference.
Addition to be made towards future prospects 12.

As the functional disability of the claim petitioner has been assessed as 20% and the claim petitioner, being a motor mechanic, I find that 40% of his established income is liable to be added towards future prospects while computing compensation for 2025:KER:59770 MACA NO. 462 OF 2020 permanent disability.
Loss of earnings 13.
The claim petitioner was hospitalized for a period of 33 days.
In the light of the injuries sustained, which include three fractures, and the period of hospitalization, in all probability, he might have been unable to work for a period of 10 months.

Therefore, I find that he can be granted compensation towards loss of earnings for a period of 10 months, that is 1,00,000/- (10,000 x 10 months).
14.
